W5 (contrarian), after E044. The tip is E036 (5.314 s, seeds 0–2 at 0.7532).

1. Rebuild noise is central, and my misses confirm it. The same commit 60645dd has read 0.7532 (E036), 0.7525 (E038) and 0.7497 (E043). E042 read 0.7549, which may also be noise. I missed 4 of the last 10 accuracy forecasts because my ranges were too narrow. max-autotune and cuDNN benchmark pick different kernels on each build, and the fp16/bf16 trajectories then diverge chaotically. So a fresh build plus seeds 0–2 gives a draw with an SD of about 0.2 pp around a population mean of about 0.752. From now on my 80% ranges are about ±0.35 pp, centred near 0.752. Only about 35% of accuracy-neutral changes clear the 0.753 gate.

2. Exchange-rate frontier. Trims cost about 0.07–0.1 pp per 0.1 s: E031, E033, E037, E039, E040 and E041 all lie on it. Accuracy tracks useful update signal, roughly the step share × the share of the network the update reaches. Two kinds of change sit off the frontier:
   - pure overhead removal;
   - changes that help averaging or calibration, but E044 (BN recalibration) gave no visible gain: 0.7519 at +0.03 s.

3. Hidden mechanism for the surprises. Under Muon with per-step renormalization, the filters' effective learning rate is fixed per step. So the knobs that matter are the step count and how the averaging ramp lines up with the end. Every tweak to the averaging or the end-point lost about 0.3–0.4 pp: E025, E030, E032, E044. The airbench Lookahead and the late schedule appear to sit at a sharp local optimum, so I expect perturbations at the end of the run to hurt more than they help.

4. Time is reproducible to ±0.02 s and predicted well by pixel and step accounting. Per-step fixed overhead is about 3–4 ms (Muon NS on many small matrices, the Python loop, the lerps). Group-1 conv1 is only about 6% of MACs (26.6M of ~450M per image), so even at poor efficiency it is probably under 10% of the step. Group 2 is compute-bound and carries most of the features.

5. The tip's population mean (~0.752) is probably at or below the gate. A further cut needs real accuracy behind it, and no booster has delivered that yet. The best remaining moves are:
   - variance control (pin the autotune choices, average several builds);
   - more steps in the cheap early phase (I068), if its added overhead stays under about 0.2 s.

Unsure: the paired offline E044 result (only seeds 0–2 are visible to me); how the PCIe judge weighs bandwidth-bound levers.

forecasts.reason: Adds about 69 steps at roughly 3–4 ms of overhead each (+0.2–0.3 s). The extra early steps may buy about +0.1 pp, but that is buried under rebuild noise, and the trade only matches the epoch dial at best.
Group 2 is the main feature block and is compute-bound. Annealing it from 75% and freezing it at 90% removes real late signal, so the expected loss is about 0.2 pp, consistent with the E037 cliff.
Conv1 is only about 6% of MACs. Even at poor efficiency I expect it to be under 10% of step time, and the larger stem cost to be pool/elementwise bandwidth.
This should give about −4.5% time but sits on the frontier, so I expect a loss of about 0.15 pp on the 20-seed mean, beyond the 0.1 pp allowance.
cuDNN already pads channels_last fp16 internally, and the padding adds traffic at 31×31. I expect a change of at most ±1%, well short of the 2% bar, plus a new rebuild draw on accuracy.

cruxes: If the autotune and cuDNN kernel choices are pinned, are seeds 0–2 bit-reproducible across builds? And what is the E036 population mean across several builds and 20 or more seeds: above or below 0.753?
What is the per-step fixed overhead (Muon NS, the Python loop, Lookahead) in ms at 20 px, batch 1000 vs 2000? This decides whether I068's extra steps cost under 0.2 s.
Did E044's paired offline test show any BN-recalibration gain, i.e. is end-point calibration a real lever, or does the averaging sit at a sharp optimum?
